title: Lifecycle sprint: creative + copy review (onboarding emails + retargeting)
topics: Onboarding email sequence v1: subject lines, CTAs, cadence, suppression and deliverability notes
Retargeting creative: claims (latency/cost/reliability), proof points, and landing page expectations
CTA debate: deep-linking into Console vs Quickstart docs vs “copy/paste cURL”
Troubleshooting messaging: auth errors, rate limits, streaming disconnects, model selection confusion
Measurement: UTMs, event attribution, and guardrails (unsubscribes, support volume)
summary: Team reviewed onboarding email copy (5-email series) and retargeting ad concepts for the lifecycle growth experiments sprint. Main debate was around CTAs: Console deep links can accelerate activation but risk 404s/route changes and confusion for users who haven’t created an API key; docs/quickstart CTAs are safer but may add steps. Group agreed to keep Email #1 and retargeting ads focused on “first successful request” with a copy-paste cURL path, while later emails can push streaming + cost dashboard. Troubleshooting content should be more explicit (401/403 key issues, 429 rate limits, streaming websocket disconnects) and should point to a single canonical troubleshooting page. Product marketing flagged benchmark claims need substantiation links and to avoid hard numbers unless Ethan provides a public reference. Tyler confirmed UTM conventions and event capture requirements (click -> console session -> activation events) and asked design to ensure ad/landing page messaging matches in-console checklist wording.
questions: Do we define activation as first 2xx completion, first streaming success, or first dashboard view for the primary email CTA?
Can we safely deep-link to the Console project setup route without creating more 404/support tickets if routing changes?
Which benchmark claims are allowed in paid ads (latency/cost) and what is the required public substantiation link?

Tyler Benson - confirm final UTM parameters + landing page URL structure and share with Marketing Ops + Eng for event stitching - due 2025-01-17
Marissa Cole - confirm Console deep-link destinations for email CTAs (stable routes) and provide fallback links if user has no project yet - due 2025-01-20
Alicia Perez - review landing page hero hierarchy: quickstart first, benchmarks second, troubleshooting third; propose layout tweaks - due 2025-01-20
next_steps: Finalize email copy v1 by end of week and route for sign-off (PMM + Design + Growth).
Lock retargeting claims to substantiated statements; avoid hard latency numbers unless Ethan provides a public source.
Create one canonical troubleshooting destination and ensure email/nudge links point there.
Confirm Console deep links and add a safe fallback to docs if user is not yet set up.
Send updated creative/copy to Tyler for UTM + attribution mapping review.
transcript:
Meeting header
Title: Lifecycle sprint: creative + copy review (onboarding emails + retargeting)
Date: 2025-01-16
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ben Carter, Tyler Benson, Soojin Lee, Ethan Wallace, Tessa Morgan, Kenji Nakamura, Alicia Perez, Marissa Cole

Summary (auto)
- Reviewed onboarding email series copy and retargeting ad concepts.
- Main open items: CTA destinations, troubleshooting messaging, benchmark claim substantiation.

Topics (auto)
1) Email sequence v1
2) Retargeting creative
3) Landing page expectations
4) Measurement + UTMs

Action items (auto)
- Update subject line A/B list and CTA hierarchy
- Confirm benchmark claim policy
- Confirm console deep links + fallbacks

Transcript

[00:00] Ben Carter: Cool, thanks everyone. This is the creative and copy review for the lifecycle sprint. Goal today is to get to “v1 ready to launch” for the five-email series and the retargeting ads. We’ve got some comments on CTAs and troubleshooting, so let’s just go straight there.

[00:18] Soojin Lee: Yep. I’ll share what changed. Email one is the welcome, right now the CTA says “Go to Console” and then we have a secondary “Read Quickstart.” A bunch of the reviews are basically like, that’s too many choices.

[00:33] Tessa Morgan: And also the “Go to Console” button is a little ambiguous. Like, does it land on a dashboard with five things? Or does it land on the exact step they need.

[00:44] Marissa Cole: The dashboard is… I mean it depends. If they have no project it prompts them, but the route is not super stable. We changed it last month.

[00:55] Tyler Benson: This is the part that makes me nervous from attribution and broken-link standpoint. If we deep-link to a route that’s behind auth and onboarding state, we can lose them and then the email click looks “successful” but activation doesn’t move.

[01:11] Ben Carter: So what’s the alternative? Make the first CTA the copy-paste cURL snippet page?

[01:18] Soojin Lee: That’s my preference. Like “Run your first request” with a copy/paste. Then after they do that, Email 3 or 4 can push “Enable streaming” or “View your cost dashboard.”

[01:31] Kenji Nakamura: The in-console checklist we’re designing is literally those steps: create API key, first request, streaming, view latency/cost. If email CTA wording matches the checklist wording, it’s less cognitive load.

[01:46] Alicia Perez: Agree. Also for the landing page variant, we can mirror the checklist. Like a four-step visual. But it means we need to settle what the step names are.

[01:57] Ben Carter: OK. Let’s talk about the CTA debate explicitly. Option A: Console deep link. Option B: Docs quickstart. Option C: Dedicated landing page with cURL and troubleshooting. What do we think is highest probability of first success in 24 hours.

[02:16] Marissa Cole: Console deep link is fastest if it works. But state handling is tricky. Some people don’t have an API key, some don’t have a project, and some are in an org that requires SSO and they bounce.

[02:30] Tyler Benson: Also, if they hit SSO wall, we should have it counted as “started sign-in” event, otherwise it’s invisible. Not sure that’s in the taxonomy.

[02:39] Kenji Nakamura: Wait, do we want Email 1 to push API key creation? Or first request? Because if they don’t have the key, they can’t do anything.

[02:48] Soojin Lee: In Email 1 body we say “Create an API key in 60 seconds” and then “Run your first request.” But the button is currently “Go to Console.” It’s basically asking them to do two things with one button.

[03:03] Ethan Wallace: From messaging standpoint, it’s cleaner if we anchor on “first successful request.” That’s like the ‘aha’. The API key is just a prerequisite step.

[03:12] Ben Carter: Right. And our activation metric discussion was trending toward first 2xx completion, not necessarily streaming.

[03:20] Soojin Lee: Exactly. But then for retargeting ads, we’re currently saying “Get streaming tokens in under a second” and I don’t love that claim.

[03:30] Ethan Wallace: Yeah, careful. We can say “low latency streaming” but not “under a second” unless we’re willing to cite a specific benchmark and conditions.

[03:39] Tyler Benson: Paid ads are where we get flagged the most. If the claim is not substantiated publicly, it’s risky. Also Soojin had a note about avoiding superlatives.

[03:49] Soojin Lee: Yeah. Devs hate it and also it invites “prove it.” Better to say something like “Predictable latency and cost controls for production inference” and then link to a benchmarks page.

[04:02] Alicia Perez: But we need a clear hook. Otherwise retargeting ads look like generic infra.

[04:09] Tessa Morgan: The hook could be “First request in 5 minutes” which is more about onboarding. That’s something we can own.

[04:18] Ben Carter: That’s interesting. But again, can we back that up? Like, if they follow the quickstart, is it truly 5 minutes? Or 15.

[04:27] Marissa Cole: With the newest SDK snippet it’s pretty fast, but if they hit environment variable issues, it’s not.

[04:35] Kenji Nakamura: That’s why troubleshooting messaging matters. The current email series has a “Need help?” line but it’s vague.

[04:44] Soojin Lee: Right now Email 2 subject line variant is “Stuck on auth?” and the body mentions “401 and 403.” But people asked if that’s too technical for the top of funnel.

[04:55] Ben Carter: For devs it’s not too technical. I think it’s reassuring. Like, it signals we know what you’re dealing with.

[05:03] Tyler Benson: Plus it can reduce support if we send them to the right page. As long as we don’t imply “contact us” as the primary path.

[05:12] Tessa Morgan: I want to make sure the troubleshooting page is not a huge wall of text. It should be like: symptom, error code, fix.

[05:21] Marissa Cole: We can link to docs troubleshooting section. There’s a PR in docs to add “common errors” but it’s not merged yet.

[05:28] Ben Carter: OK, so decision: Email #1 CTA is “Run your first request” and it goes to either quickstart docs or the landing page that includes cURL.

[05:39] Soojin Lee: I’m leaning landing page. Because ads and emails can share the same destination. It’s consistent. And it’s not gated.

[05:49] Tyler Benson: From attribution, a single landing page is easier. UTM in, then we can set a cookie and pass it to Console if they click “Open Console.” We’re implementing UTM propagation soon.

[06:01] Kenji Nakamura: But if we do landing page, we need to ensure the “Open Console” button doesn’t dump them somewhere confusing.

[06:09] Alicia Perez: We can make the landing page step 1 be “Create API key” with a button that goes to Console key page.

[06:17] Marissa Cole: That link is more stable. The API key page route hasn’t changed in a while. I can confirm the exact path and provide a fallback.

[06:26] Ben Carter: Great. Let’s talk retargeting ad concepts. Tessa, you had three frames.

[06:32] Tessa Morgan: Yeah. Concept A is “Stop paying for idle GPUs” with a cost angle. Concept B is “Production inference without the yak shave” more dev-experience. Concept C is “Predictable latency” with a benchmark-y vibe.

[06:48] Ethan Wallace: The cost angle is good but it can sound like we’re a hosting provider. We need to still communicate reliability and controls.

[06:57] Soojin Lee: Also, “Stop paying for idle GPUs” is more relevant to Dedicated. Our sprint is targeting self-serve hosted API activation.

[07:06] Ben Carter: Right. Our audience is signups who didn’t activate, or lapsed. They may not be thinking about idle GPUs yet.

[07:14] Tyler Benson: And from channel perspective, LinkedIn vs Google, the messaging should be more straightforward on Google. Like “LLM inference API quickstart.” LinkedIn can handle a more narrative angle.

[07:26] Alicia Perez: Can we do a concept that’s literally a snippet? Like “curl …” in the creative.

[07:33] Kenji Nakamura: That actually works with dev audiences. It signals “this is for builders.”

[07:40] Soojin Lee: I like it, but we have to ensure the snippet is correct and minimal. No huge payload.

[07:48] Ethan Wallace: And we should avoid including a real API endpoint that might change. Also no fake claims in the snippet.

[07:55] Ben Carter: Could be pseudo-code. Like “curl /v1/chat/completions” type.

[08:01] Marissa Cole: Our API path is stable, but please don’t include anything that suggests a specific model name that’s region-limited.

[08:10] Tyler Benson: Another consideration: ad policy. Some platforms don’t like code blocks in images, but we can do it as text ad or as a simplified graphic.

[08:20] Tessa Morgan: OK, so retargeting direction: “first request” oriented, less benchmark heavy, but we can still have a secondary line “low latency streaming” without numbers.

[08:32] Soojin Lee: Yes, and we can add “benchmarks in docs” with a link. Ethan, we need approved benchmark links. Like blog or docs page, not internal sheet.

[08:42] Ethan Wallace: I can pull the public benchmark post and make sure it’s up to date. But I want to gate what we claim. Like “competitive” not “fastest.”

[08:53] Ben Carter: Great. Now troubleshooting messaging. What are the top issues we’ve heard? I know auth errors.

[09:00] Kenji Nakamura: Auth and also rate limits. People hit 429 and assume it’s broken.

[09:06] Marissa Cole: Also streaming disconnect. The web socket closes and they think Redwood is unstable, but it’s often a client timeout or proxy.

[09:16] Alicia Perez: And model selection confusion. They pick a model that’s not recommended for their region or they don’t know which to use.

[09:24] Soojin Lee: For Email 2 I propose we literally say: “If you see 401/403: check key permissions. If 429: check rate limits. If request hangs: try non-streaming first.”

[09:39] Ben Carter: That’s good. The only risk is it becomes a support doc in email.

[09:44] Tyler Benson: But short bullets are fine. Also include a single “Troubleshooting” CTA, not five links.

[09:51] Tessa Morgan: Agree. We should avoid ‘choose your own adventure’ in email. One primary action.

[10:00] Ben Carter: OK, subjects. What’s the A/B for Email 1?

[10:04] Soojin Lee: Variant A: “Welcome to Redwood — your first request in minutes” Variant B: “Your API key + first request (quickstart)” Variant C: “Ship LLM inference with predictable latency”

[10:18] Ethan Wallace: C feels too marketing-y. A or B are more direct.

[10:24] Kenji Nakamura: “API key + first request” is super clear. Might reduce opens though.

[10:30] Tyler Benson: We can test. But deliverability wise, avoid too many symbols. The plus sign sometimes triggers weird preview text.

[10:39] Soojin Lee: Good point, we can do “API key and first request.”

[10:44] Ben Carter: Nice. Retargeting CTA should match: “Run your first request” not “Learn more.”

[10:52] Alicia Perez: For landing page, do we want “Copy/paste” above the fold?

[10:56] Tessa Morgan: Yes. Above the fold is a code snippet and a “Get API key” button. Below is benchmarks and then troubleshooting.

[11:08] Marissa Cole: Please make sure “Get API key” requires login, but that’s fine. We can also show “No account? Sign up” path.

[11:15] Tyler Benson: On UTMs: if the landing page sends them to Console, we need to preserve utm_source, campaign, content. The PR is in flight but we should assume it’s ready by launch.

[11:27] Ben Carter: Also guardrails. If we become too aggressive on troubleshooting, we might increase support link clicks. But that could be OK if activation increases.

[11:36] Kenji Nakamura: Or we can add “common fixes” and only then link to support.

[11:42] Soojin Lee: For compliance, we need to be careful about “reply to this email” as support. Better to direct to help center.

[11:50] Tyler Benson: Yes, and also suppression rules: once they opt out they should not get retargeted via email. Ads are separate, but email suppression has to be airtight.

[12:00] Ben Carter: OK. Let’s do a quick pass through each email with the new CTA philosophy.

[12:06] Soojin Lee: Email 1: Welcome + quickstart. Primary CTA: “Run your first request.” Secondary text link: “Open Console.”

[12:17] Ben Carter: I would invert that. Primary “Run your first request” to landing page. Secondary “Create API key” to console key page.

[12:26] Marissa Cole: That’s fine.

[12:28] Soojin Lee: Email 2: Troubleshooting / unblock. Subject variants: “Stuck on auth?” vs “Common setup fixes (401/429)” Primary CTA: “Troubleshooting.”

[12:41] Tessa Morgan: Keep it short. Don’t include too many screenshots. Some clients clip images.

[12:47] Tyler Benson: Also images can hurt deliverability. Limit to one.

[12:52] Soojin Lee: Email 3: Streaming. CTA: “Enable streaming” and link to docs example.

[13:00] Kenji Nakamura: Also maybe “Try the streaming example” with a code snippet.

[13:06] Ethan Wallace: Streaming messaging: avoid “real-time” unless we define it. Just say “token-by-token streaming.”

[13:14] Soojin Lee: Email 4: Cost/latency dashboard. CTA: “View your latency and cost.”

[13:22] Alicia Perez: I’ll provide a screenshot that shows the tokens/latency breakdown, but keep it anonymized.

[13:29] Tyler Benson: Make sure the dashboard screenshot matches what’s actually in Console next week.

[13:34] Marissa Cole: That’s tricky. The dashboard is stable, but we’re shipping a banner and checklist. I’ll confirm the layout.

[13:43] Soojin Lee: Email 5: Next steps / invite teammate / add billing. CTA: “Invite a teammate” or “Add billing to remove limits.”

[13:55] Ben Carter: For week 1–2 retention, pushing billing might be too early. But as a secondary CTA maybe.

[14:03] Tyler Benson: Also if billing add is a metric, we should track it, but I’d keep it late.

[14:09] Soojin Lee: OK. Retargeting ads should align with Email 1: “Run your first request.”

[14:17] Tessa Morgan: Agreed. And landing page should match.

[14:21] Ben Carter: Any concerns about saying “production” in the ads?

[14:26] Soojin Lee: I’m okay with “production-grade inference” but don’t overpromise enterprise features. Like don’t imply VPC or SOC2 in this flow unless we link to the right pages.

[14:37] Ethan Wallace: Yeah, and “SLA” can be tricky. Hosted self-serve doesn’t have enterprise SLA. Keep it to reliability and fallbacks.

[14:47] Marissa Cole: Also if we say “audit logs” it implies enterprise plan. So avoid in paid.

[14:53] Ben Carter: OK. So ad copy: “Developer-first LLM inference. Run your first request in minutes. Low-latency streaming. Cost and latency dashboards.” No numbers.

[15:06] Alicia Perez: For visuals: one concept with a snippet, one with a checklist, one with a dashboard screenshot.

[15:14] Tyler Benson: Make sure screenshot doesn’t reveal customer data. Also, if we use dashboard, ensure it’s not confusing what the units are.

[15:23] Kenji Nakamura: I prefer the checklist visual. It sets expectation: do these steps.

[15:30] Tessa Morgan: Great. I’ll refine three creatives.

[15:34] Ben Carter: Last topic: what do we link as proof point? Ethan.

[15:38] Ethan Wallace: I’ll send the benchmark blog link and maybe a docs page about performance. But I’ll need to review what’s current.

[15:48] Soojin Lee: And in ad copy we can say “See benchmarks” as a secondary link.

[15:54] Tyler Benson: If we do multiple links, we need separate UTMs for each so we know what’s driving activation.

[16:03] Ben Carter: OK, we can keep one link per ad for now. Otherwise attribution is messy.

[16:08] Tyler Benson: Great, thanks.

[16:10] Ben Carter: Anything else on troubleshooting? I want to ensure we’re not sending users to generic support.

[16:17] Marissa Cole: If we can add a short “If you see 401, check key; 403, permissions; 429, rate limit” in the console error banners too, it’ll help.

[16:27] Kenji Nakamura: That’s in the nudge copy deck. I’ll align it with the email wording.

[16:34] Tessa Morgan: We should avoid blame-y language. Like “you did this wrong.” More like “Common causes.”

[16:42] Soojin Lee: Yes. “If you’re seeing…” language.

[16:47] Ben Carter: Cool. Let’s recap decisions and owners.

[16:52] Ben Carter: Decision one: primary CTA is “Run your first request” and it goes to the activation landing page with cURL + API key step + troubleshooting. Decision two: retargeting claims avoid numbers; include “benchmarks” only with approved link. Decision three: troubleshooting bullets in Email 2 with one canonical troubleshooting page.

[17:14] Tyler Benson: And I’ll send UTM conventions and confirm we can propagate UTMs into Console events.

[17:20] Ethan Wallace: I’ll send benchmark substantiation link set.

[17:24] Marissa Cole: I’ll confirm stable Console deep links for API key creation and any onboarding route we use.

[17:31] Tessa Morgan: I’ll revise creative directions accordingly.

[17:35] Soojin Lee: I’ll update email copy and subject line variants and send for sign-off.

[17:42] Ben Carter: Great. We’ll reconvene briefly tomorrow async in Slack unless something blocks. Thanks everyone.

[17:50] Speaker 1: Thanks.

[17:51] Speaker 2: Bye.
